hard_case: `toThrow("limit ")` is a substring match, which both `limit 5` and `limit ` contain

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the message changes from `limit 5` to `limit `, but `toThrow("limit ")` only asks that the message contain `limit `, which both do

reasoning: `throw new RangeError("limit " + max)` drops `+ max`. The test calls `limitMessage(10, 5)` and asserts `toThrow("limit ")`; a string argument to `toThrow` matches any message that contains it, so `limit 5` and `limit ` both pass. RIPR-SPEC-0248 example 10: the error seam is outside the dropped-term rule. Since the 2026-10-14 RIPR-SPEC-0243 rule 4 amendment the change is message-only, and `toThrow("limit ")` cannot be shown to match exactly one of the two messages, so ripr reports `weakly_exposed`, the ideal gap. At labeling it reported `exposed` with exact_error_variant / strong, a false exposed verdict.
